evidence.quote: Some books when not (books.Books.Customers.IsEmpty && books.Books.Drafts.IsEmpty && books.Books.Invoices.IsEmpty && books.Payments.IsEmpty)

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new domain rules are decided in Tier 2. Transfer.read (Summa.Storage) decides the schema, version, snapshot-check and data-version rules. The engine (Summa.Web.Engine) decides the new-books-only rule, the GitHub refusal, the downloads-pack requirement and the file name. Tier 3 only adds three event-name mappings in AccountingWire.fs, which forward to Msg cases and decide nothing.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The export time comes from ctx.Now, so the existing message context supplies the clock. The date in the file name comes from model.Today. The download is requested as an existing OfferDownload effect, and the import is persisted through the existing save helper (SaveBooks). No clock, randomness or I/O is read below Tier 4. Transfer.fs opens System.IO and System.Text.Json and uses MemoryStream and Utf8JsonWriter, which ARC-SYM-01 lists as symbols Tier 1/2 may not use. They are used in memory only, with no external effect, so this is a rule-text concern and not an effect-flow breach.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The schema name, version and timestamp format are each defined once, as Schema, Version and stampFormat in Transfer.fs. The classification comes from Exports.Classification and the data version from Exports.dataVersion, so neither is restated. The 'yyyy-MM-dd' literal appears twice in Accounting.fs, once for the download name's business date and once for the export's UTC date. These are two different facts, not a copy of one fact.

evidence.quote: let counts (r: Receivables) = r.Books.Customers.Count, r.Books.Invoices.Count, r.Payments.Count

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The contents-versus-books rule and the version acceptance live in Transfer.read (Tier 2). The preview, including its readability decision and pluralisation, is in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2) and calls Transfer.read and Transfer.counts. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code decides anything; the HTML only binds the view value.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no new effect. The preview is a pure function of the pasted text and goes into the view projection. The contents counts are written by the same pure export function. The reads happen in Tier 2 and are in-memory only.

evidence.quote: | Some v when v <> "1" && v <> "2" -> Error $"Transfer files of version {v} cannot be read here."
| Error why -> $"This file cannot be imported: {why}"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have one definition, Transfer.counts, which export, read and the preview all use. The set of supported versions is restated as the literals "1" and "2" in read, next to the Version literal, and the contents check hardcodes "2". A future version bump could drift from these copies, but they currently agree. The 'This file cannot be imported: ' prefix is also written both in the import handler (change set 1) and in the preview. Those copies agree too.
